failure_summary: The L3 link text render_decision.link.text over-claims the grain of opponentPunishment.tag=immediate_threat — it asserts "the threat to make four next move at c5r4 is coming no matter what you play here", but on the assembled prompt s own afterBest board (movestring 3152332536215522346266536411) column 5 still has height 2 so c5r4 is not reachable next move and that board block itself lists only "major at c5r4 (opp)", and 3 of 5 runs echoed the over-claim into the board-false claim that column 2 answers/pressures/meets that next-move four.
notes: Sub-sampling applied per rubric: A3, A4, G2, G4, G5 scored on runs 0-1 only; runs 2-4 are null (not scored) on those axes. A5 and A7 scored on all 5 runs. A1/A2/A6 and G7a/G7b membership copied verbatim from fv_suff_answers_boards_subset_2026-08-26T15-47-56Z_mechanical.json (all pass); annotationRepairs is [] on all 5 runs so no G7c auto-fail, and every emitted handle wraps shape-matched words (square words on the c5r4 single-square handle, line words on the windows:c7r2,c6r3,c5r4,c4r5 handle), so G7 passes on judgment too. | A4 run 0: "your opponent still has to answer the threat to make four next move at c5r4" inverts ownership — c5r4 is the OPPONENT s winning square; after the better move (col 2) gray s only major threat is c1r3, so there is nothing there for the opponent to answer. Contributing seed: the prompt s afterPlayed tactics block legitimately lists BOTH "immediate at c5r4 (opp)" and "immediate at c5r4 (you)" (board-true — gray completes c5r1-r4 vertically there), which invites the ownership mix-up when the model transposes it onto the afterBest branch. | A4 run 1: "your opponent s next-move four at c5r4" attributed to the column-2 branch is board-false for the same reason, and "column 2 keeps the pressure on" that threat is not a thing column 2 does (col 2 lands at c2r4 and touches neither c5r4 nor its diagonal). | A7a runs 0, 1, 3: the mechanism never says what column 5 actually did (it fills c5r3, the square directly under the opponent s winning square, turning a non-reachable major threat into a gravity-top immediate win — visualize_board.sh on 3152332536215522346266536414 shows col5 row4 as <*> [GT], solver 7). All three collapse to a pure speed comparison ("gives that line up sooner", "finish more directly", "a simpler path to the same finish"), which leaves the blunderer with no transferable idea. Run 3 additionally manufactures specificity — "column 2 meets your opponent s next-move four at c5r4" is board-false — but A4 was not scored on run 3 under the sub-sample. | Runs 2 and 4 pass every scored axis: both name the real cause ("the spot that lets your opponent cash in on that key square", "keeps your reply from opening up your opponent s next-move four on that square") and both avoid raw cNrM in prose. NOTE run 4 sits against the L3 guardrail ("MUST NOT say the played move caused or enabled the pattern") — G2 was not scored on run 4 under the sub-sample, but the tension is real and is the flip side of the same render defect: the guardrail forbids the one true, teachable causal statement (the move made the pattern REACHABLE, which is not the same as creating it), so the compliant runs are the uninformative ones. | Known-open, seen and not treated as new: OI-194 — raw cNrM leaks into player-facing prose in runs 0, 1 and 3 ("the square at c5r4", "c7r2, c6r3, c5r4, and c4r5"); not failed under A5a because the frozen v1 banned-vocabulary list does not enumerate coordinate notation. OI-183 — the harness calls the model once with no retry; not load-bearing here since the required set (opp-major-3, opp-major-line-3) was emitted in all 5 runs. | Branch-invariance / patternOnAfterBestBoard=true and the L3 route were consumed as ground truth for routing and NOT recomputed, per Step 0; G6 passes on that basis. The finding above is about the link TEXT s grain, not the routing bit. | Model regime: gpt-5.4-mini, the production model — a production-fidelity run, so any prompt_confusion attribution could not be separated from model capability; the decisive triage chosen here (render_bug) is model-independent and survives a change of model.

counterexamples.field_or_glossary: render_decision.link.text (L3) + terms.immediate_threat canonicalPhrase "threat to make four next move"
counterexamples.evidence: Assembled prompt (assembleGroundedPrompt(buildReasonRenderModel(fv))) says "Your opponent s threat to make four next move at c5r4 is coming no matter what you play here". On the afterBest board 3152332536215522346266536411 col5 height is 2 (c5r3 empty), no green cell is gravity-top-winning, and the prompt s own afterBest Tactics block lists "major at c5r4 (opp)" — NOT "immediate". The next-move grain is true only on afterPlayed 3152332536215522346266536414, where visualize_board.sh marks col5 row4 <*> [GT].

counterexamples.field_or_glossary: opponentPunishment.owner (=1) vs the afterPlayed dual-owner tactics line "immediate at c5r4 (you)"
counterexamples.evidence: Run 0 tells the player the OPPONENT must answer the c5r4 threat. On afterBest the only gray major threat is c1r3 (visualize_board.sh, Major threats: col1 row3 (O)); c5r4 belongs to green there. Gray does share c5r4 on afterPlayed (vertical c5r1-c5r4), which is what the render renders, but green moves first and wins it.

counterexamples.field_or_glossary: render_decision.link.guardrail (L3) — "MUST NOT say the played move caused or enabled the pattern"
counterexamples.evidence: The true teachable cause is reachability, not creation: col 5 fills c5r3 (Decision block: "Played move: column 5 (lands at c5r3)"), converting a non-gravity-top major at c5r4 into a gravity-top immediate win (solver 7 on 3152332536215522346266536414 vs max 6 on 3152332536215522346266536411; replyHistogram 1 vs 5). The blanket guardrail suppresses that statement, and the three runs that obeyed it most literally (0, 1, 3) produced speed-only prose with no transferable idea.
